Write down a product allowance, a shipping allowance and an amount you are comfortable setting aside for optional services or changes. Use current quotations rather than a fixed percentage copied from another person’s order. A light but bulky product and a compact heavy product can produce different shipping quotes.

Write down the order reference and the latest status before asking for a change. Is your question about an item still being purchased, an item already received at the warehouse, or a parcel that has been dispatched? Giving the stage helps support identify the applicable process.

Write down the size, color, style and quantity beside the ID. If the original listing includes several styles, verify the chosen option rather than comparing only the default price shown when the page opens.

Write down whether your main constraint is cost, a target arrival window, packaging or a particular service requirement. If you have a deadline, leave room for the stages before international dispatch as well. Your shortlist is easier to evaluate when you know what would make an option unsuitable.

Write down which items you intend to include in the parcel and which packing decisions you still need to make. If several items are involved, do not assume they have all reached the same stage. Compare your intended contents with the parcel information actually shown.
